name: pnp-sharepoint-skills-resume-screening-summarizer
title: Resume Screening Summarizer
shortDescription: Screens a library of resumes against a job description's must-have and nice-to-have criteria and produces a ranked, color-coded HTML shortlist report.
longDescription: Hiring teams often collect dozens of resumes for an open role in a SharePoint library, then manually re-read each one against the job description. The Resume Screening Summarizer reads the job description and every resume or application in a specified library, extracts each candidate's relevant qualifications, and scores them against the stated must-have and nice-to-have criteria.

Each candidate is placed into a fit tier — Strong match, Possible match, Weak match, or Not scored (unreadable file) — with the must-haves and nice-to-haves met, and a one-line rationale grounded in the candidate's actual resume text. The exact scoring criteria are included in the report so reviewers can audit every result.

The output is a fully self-contained HTML report — no scripts, no external assets — saved to a Resume Screening Reports folder with a timestamped filename. The skill is strictly read-only: it never contacts candidates, modifies resumes, or alters any content beyond the saved report.

Tested against a batch of 20+ synthetic resumes screened against an Amazon-style job description, covering edge cases such as alternate frameworks (Vue/Angular accepted alongside React), ambiguous degree fields, resumes where total job tenure doesn't match the relevant experience described, and image-only PDFs with no extractable text.
